# Every line below MUST produce NO match from _ss_scan_content.
#
# This half of the corpus is the one that earns its keep. Making the opening
# quote optional (#1755) widened the pattern into three new false-positive
# classes, and the gate blocks on a match — a false positive here is a build
# that cannot merge. Each class below is represented deliberately.
#
# '#' comment lines and blank lines are skipped by the corpus sweep.

# ── variable references, no space: the only negative the original had ────────
token=$SECRET_ENV
api_key=$MY_KEY_VAR

# ── variable references WITH whitespace before the $ ─────────────────────────
# `[[:space:]]*` can match zero characters, so a value class that permits a
# space lets the leading `[^$...]` eat the space and match the $VAR anyway.
# This class defeated the guard on every workflow env block in the repo.
token: $SECRET_ENV
token= $SECRET_ENV
api_key = $MY_KEY_VAR
password:  ${SECRET}
secret:   ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}

# ── bare keyword with no value ───────────────────────────────────────────────
password=
token:
api_key =

# ── short values below the 8-char floor ──────────────────────────────────────
password=short
token: abc123
api_key="tiny"

# ── prose and documentation mentions ─────────────────────────────────────────
The password is stored in the vault, ask an admin.
# password: please contact the administrator for access
Set your api_key: see the docs for how to obtain one
password = <your password here>

# ── code that merely assigns to a variable named like a credential ───────────
            token  = substr(rest, RSTART, RLENGTH)
local token = shift(args, offset)
secret = compute(seed, salt)
